t: No appropriation or fund made available or authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall be used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during the fiscal year 1979.

fable.w: This is a restriction on how continuing-resolution appropriations may be used, barring new or resumed projects that were not funded in fiscal year 1979. The words "project or activity" might suggest some outside involvement, but no party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object. It only limits federal spending authority, so there is no participation.
fable.s: shall be used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during the fiscal year 1979

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that limits the use of appropriated funds to projects that were already authorized in the previous fiscal year. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. It is purely an internal budgetary constraint.
qwen_block.s: No appropriation or fund made available or authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall be used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during the fiscal year 1979.

opus.w: This is a funding restriction. Money and authority under the joint resolution can't be used to start or resume projects that lacked funding or authority in fiscal year 1979. No outside party is consulted or given a comment period, hearing, advisory role or right to sue. Words like "authority granted" are standard appropriations wording and don't create any process that brings outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.b: **Step 1 (thinking):** The tempting reading is that "authority granted" points to some decision-making process. It doesn't. This is a standard limit in a continuing appropriations resolution: funds can't be used to start or resume projects that had no funding or authority in fiscal year 1979. No one outside the federal government is consulted, asked to comment, given a hearing or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a fiscal restriction prohibiting the use of funds for projects not previously funded. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties, nor does it create advisory bodies or public comment periods. The text solely limits executive action based on prior fiscal availability.
qwen_chat.s: No appropriation or fund made available or authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall be used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were not available during the fiscal year 1979.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the restriction on using funds implies a need for oversight or consultation to determine if a project was funded in 1979, but the text itself contains no mechanism for such consultation. It is purely a fiscal restriction.
